domain.description: The domain, like example.com or www.example.com.

tools.name: ploa_web_domain_check
tools.description: Checks the domains connected to a site now: whether the TXT proves each is the person's, whether its A or CNAME sends it to Ploa, and whether a request reaches Ploa's hosting; with the records still to add and what's wrong. DNS changes usually show within minutes, sometimes hours; Ploa also checks by itself every few minutes. Read-only for the person's DNS.

site.description: The site's address (the part before .ploa.app) or ID. Needed when the workspace has more than one site.

domain.description: One domain to check (default: all of the site's).

tools.name: ploa_web_rollback
tools.description: Puts a site back on a version that was live before (the one before the current, or the one named), at once and with no review: it's how to undo a bad release. Ploa keeps the last 10 versions' files. Tell the person which version it goes back to.

site.description: The site's address (the part before .ploa.app) or ID. Needed when the workspace has more than one site.

version.description: The version's build number (13) or ID, as ploa_web_status lists them.

tools.name: ploa_server_status
tools.description: The app's server, the server side of its web app: an API, scheduled jobs and a Postgres database Ploa runs on Google Cloud, either in Ploa's cloud (on Pro and Team, one for each app, its room set by the plan; nothing is bought) or in the person's own Google Cloud project (any plan, Google bills them). Says where it stands, its address, the live version and the last deploys, its variables (secrets by name only), its jobs, and what's needed when it's stopped. With no server, the kinds the workspace can have. Read-only. Start here.

dir.description: The app's folder (absolute path). Defaults to the folder the agent runs in.

tools.name: ploa_server_create
tools.description: Makes the app's server, the server side of its web app. cloud: ploa (on Pro and Team: made at once with the room the plan gives each app; nothing is bought) or own (the person's Google Cloud project, any plan: Ploa prints commands they run once to let it in). Ask the person which before calling. retry: true carries on making one that stopped (after the person ran the commands, say). folder and releaseCommand set where the server's code is in the repository and a command run before each version goes live (database migrations, say: npx prisma migrate deploy).

dir.description: The app's folder (absolute path). Defaults to the folder the agent runs in.

project.description: For cloud: own, the Google Cloud project's ID (Settings › Builds' when not given).

region.description: For cloud: own (me-west1, Tel Aviv, when not given).

folder.description: The server's folder in the repository, such as server or apps/api.

releaseCommand.description: Run once before each version goes live; null for none.

tools.name: ploa_server_deploy
tools.description: Sends the server's code as a new version: the server's folder from the project (the default), or source: github to have Ploa take it from the app's linked repository (a commit, or the branch's head). Ploa builds it in the server's Google Cloud with its Dockerfile, or as Node, Python, Go, Java, Ruby, PHP or .NET by itself (package.json's start script, a Procfile...); it must listen on the PORT variable. Then the release command runs, and the new version goes live; the one before stays for rolling back. Returns at once: ploa_server_status says how it went, and ploa_server_logs shows the build and the server's output.

dir.description: The app's folder (absolute path). Defaults to the folder the agent runs in.

folder.description: The server's folder, relative to the app's folder; the server's own setting when not given.

tools.name: ploa_server_env
tools.description: Sets or removes the server's environment variables; the live version restarts with them. secret: true for keys and passwords (kept in Ploa's vault and Google's Secret Manager, never shown again); plain values show. Never put a secret the person hasn't given you; ask them to set it on the server's page instead. DATABASE_URL is set by Ploa.

dir.description: The app's folder (absolute path). Defaults to the folder the agent runs in.

tools.name: ploa_server_logs
tools.description: The server's output and its jobs', newest first (the last day unless since is given): what it printed, requests with their status, crashes. text finds lines with those words; job: a job's name, or run for commands run with ploa_server_run. Read-only.

dir.description: The app's folder (absolute path). Defaults to the folder the agent runs in.

tools.name: ploa_server_run
tools.description: Runs a shell command once with the server's live version, its variables and database (a seed script, a one-off fix). There's no SSH: its output is in ploa_server_logs with job: run. Needs the production tier.

dir.description: The app's folder (absolute path). Defaults to the folder the agent runs in.

tools.name: ploa_server_jobs
tools.description: Adds or changes a scheduled job (name, schedule as cron's five fields in UTC, at most every 5 minutes, and the command, run with the live version), or removes one. The package sets how many (Mini 1, S 3, M 10).

dir.description: The app's folder (absolute path). Defaults to the folder the agent runs in.

tools.name: ploa_db_query
tools.description: Runs SQL on the server's Postgres as its own role, which reaches that database only. Read-only unless write: true (needs the production tier; prefer migrations in the code for the schema). Returns the last statement's rows.

dir.description: The app's folder (absolute path). Defaults to the folder the agent runs in.

tools.name: ploa_github_status
tools.description: Where builds on GitHub stand for this app, and what's next: whether GitHub is connected to Ploa, the repository, folder (and any platform's own folder) and release branch linked, Ploa's workflow on that branch (current, older, missing; whether it still builds), each platform's build state with its reason (the same the dashboard's Build button shows), where iOS builds (the person's Mac or GitHub's Macs), build files a build would miss, and GitHub minutes. Ends with the next steps, each marked for the person (with its link) or for you. Read-only.

dir.description: The app's folder (absolute path). Defaults to the folder the agent runs in.

tools.name: ploa_github_setup
tools.description: Does your part of setting up builds on GitHub for this app and asks the person for theirs. GitHub not connected: returns the link where the person connects it (once: a trip to github.com and back). Not linked: asks to link the app to its repository, folder and release branch (read from this checkout's origin and folder unless given). The link decides which repository's runs get the app's signing, so a person approves it on ploa.dev (an autonomous agent's links at once); pass the person the link and follow it with ploa_approval_status. Linked: Ploa commits its workflow to the release branch (a pull request when the branch is protected) once the GitHub installation has approved the Workflows permission; until then it says how the file gets there (the person adds it from the app's GitHub card, or you add it in the checkout and open a pull request; its text is in the result). And what's left. Builds nothing; run ploa_github_status after.

repo.description: owner/name on GitHub. Default: this checkout's origin (or the repository already linked).

folder.description: The app's folder in the repository ("" for its top). Default: this checkout's; on the web, the folder whose app is this one.

branch.description: The release branch builds start from. Default: the repository's default branch.

dir.description: The app's folder (absolute path). Defaults to the folder the agent runs in.

tools.name: ploa_github_settings
tools.description: Asks to change the app's GitHub settings, the switches on its GitHub card in Ploa: labelBuilds (a PR label ploa:android, ploa:ios or ploa:all builds the PR's head), iosHosted (iOS builds on GitHub's Macs instead of the person's own Mac; the signing identity goes to GitHub's machine for the build, and a Mac minute counts as ten of the person's GitHub minutes on a private repository: say so first), releaseFlow (Releases on GitHub: deployments, a tag and a GitHub Release when a version goes live, the next version's PR), storeCode (the store page from the repo's store/ folder becomes drafts on push) and issues (GitHub issues from the stores per source: rejections, reviews, crashes, feedback). Give only what should change. The app must be linked to its repository first (ploa_github_setup). The settings are the person's: a person approves the change on ploa.dev, and iOS on GitHub's Macs only an owner (an autonomous agent's change goes through at once, but never iosHosted, which an owner turns on the card). Pass the person the link and follow it with ploa_approval_status. Already as asked: nothing is asked.

labelBuilds.description: Builds from PR labels (ploa:android, ploa:ios, ploa:all).

iosHosted.description: iOS builds on GitHub's Macs (true) or the person's own Mac as a self-hosted runner (false). An owner's decision.

releaseFlow.description: Releases on GitHub: deployments, a tag and a GitHub Release when a version goes live, the next version's PR.

storeCode.description: The store page from the repo's store/ folder: a push to the release branch makes drafts.

issues.description: GitHub issues from the stores, per source.

rejections.description: An issue per App Review or Play rejection, closed once approved.

reviews.description: One issue a day per store with the new one- and two-star reviews.

crashes.description: An issue while Google Play's crash or ANR rate is over its bad-behavior threshold.

feedback.description: One issue a day with TestFlight testers' feedback.

dir.description: The app's folder (absolute path). Defaults to the folder the agent runs in.

tools.name: ploa_details_get
tools.description: Everything both stores ask for, as one set of answers, the same as the person's Store details wizard on ploa.dev: the languages (each with its App Store and Google Play code), the text per language, the links and contact, category, age rating answers (with every question and its allowed answers), price and countries, App Review's contact and demo account, release, and privacy. Plus problems: what each store would refuse now (FIX) and what's likely a mistake (check), each with the step and language it's in, and what's left for the person to enter by hand in a store's console, with links. Start here; then ploa_details_save, ploa_privacy_save, and ploa_details_send.

step.description: Only one step's answers; all when left out.

fresh.description: Ask the stores again instead of the copy from the last two minutes.

dir.description: The app's folder (absolute path). Defaults to the folder the agent runs in.

tools.name: ploa_details_save
tools.description:
Saves answers as drafts in Ploa, one step at a time, for both stores at once (a token allowed to draft is enough; nothing reaches a store until ploa_details_send). Returns what each store would still refuse. step and values:
- text: { languages: { <language code from ploa_details_get, or a new one like "fr-FR">: { name (both stores, 30), subtitle (App Store, 30), shortDescription (Google Play, 80), description (both, 4000), keywords (App Store, 100, commas; Ploa tidies them), promotionalText (App Store, 170, optional), whatsNew (App Store 4000, only for an update; Google Play 500, on the next build Ploa puts on a track), whatsNewApple and whatsNewGoogle (optional: the App Store's or Google Play's own What's New in place of the shared whatsNew, when a store's notes need words the other's can't have, like its own devices; either alone changes only that store's; whatsNew again makes it one text for both) } } } — several languages in one call; ask the person which languages first.
- links: { supportUrl, marketingUrl, privacyPolicyUrl } (https; the same in every App Store language).
- contact: { email (public, Google requires it), phone, website }.
- language: { playDefaultLanguage: <language code from ploa_details_get> } — Google Play's default listing language (the store page shown where the app has none in someone's language; Play Console's Store settings). The person's decision. It must be one of the app's languages; one Play's listing doesn't have yet needs its text saved too (step text), and goes after it.
- about: { primaryCategory, secondaryCategory, contentRights: "USES_THIRD_PARTY_CONTENT" | "DOES_NOT_USE_THIRD_PARTY_CONTENT", declarations: { newsApp, healthApp, healthFeatures, financialFeatures, governmentApp } }. healthFeatures: Google Play's Health apps form is a list: activityFitness (Activity and Fitness), nutritionWeight (Nutrition and Weight Management), periodTracking (Period Tracking), sleep (Sleep Management), stressRelaxation (Stress Management, Relaxation, Mental Acuity), diseases (Diseases and Conditions Management), clinicalDecision (Clinical Decision Support), publicHealth (Disease Prevention and Public Health), emergency (Emergency and First Aid), healthcareServices (Healthcare Services and Management), mentalHealth (Mental and Behavioral Health), medicalReference (Medical Reference and Education), medication (Medication and Treatment Management), physicalTherapy (Physical Therapy and Rehabilitation), reproductive (Reproductive and Sexual Health), medicalDevice (Medical Device Apps), research (Research studies, clinical trials, and patient communities); pick each the app has (a breathing or meditation app is stressRelaxation), or [] with healthApp false.
- rating: { age: { <question>: answer } (every question; Google Play's content rating follows from it), ages: [...] (who it's for: the person's decision) }.
- price: { pricePointId (from ploa_appstore_price_points; the person's decision), everywhere: true | false, territories: ["ISR", …], sells: true | false } — an agent's price change waits for a person's approval when sent.
- review: { contactFirstName, contactLastName, contactEmail, contactPhone (+country code), demoAccountRequired, demoAccountName, demoAccountPassword, notes, copyright, releaseType: "AFTER_APPROVAL" | "MANUAL" } — App Review's contact is private and never the store page's. A file for the reviewers (a demo video, a document) goes with ploa_review_attachment_upload.

dir.description: The app's folder (absolute path). Defaults to the folder the agent runs in.

tools.name: ploa_review_attachment_upload
tools.description: Uploads a file for Apple's reviewers to the App Store version being prepared, beside the review notes: a demo video of a flow they can't reach (hardware, a paid account, a location), or a document (from an absolute path on this machine, up to 500 MB). It goes to App Store Connect straight away, not as a draft; while the version is with App Review, Ploa keeps it and sends it once Apple has decided (files over 60 MB can't wait: send them again then). ploa_details_get step review lists the attachments with their ids. Needs a token allowed to submit.

dir.description: The app's folder (absolute path). Defaults to the folder the agent runs in.

tools.name: ploa_review_attachment_remove
tools.description: Removes one App Review attachment from the App Store version being prepared, by the id ploa_details_get step review lists. While the version is with App Review, Ploa removes it once Apple has decided. Needs a token allowed to submit.

dir.description: The app's folder (absolute path). Defaults to the folder the agent runs in.

tools.name: ploa_privacy_save
tools.description: What the app collects, once for both stores: Apple's App Privacy and Google Play's Data safety are made from it. Read the app's code first (ploa_privacy_hints). apple: { collects: true|false, types: { <type>: { purposes: [appFunctionality|analytics|personalization|developerAdvertising|thirdPartyAdvertising|other], linked: bool, tracking: bool } } } with types name, email, phone, address, otherContact, health, fitness, payment, credit, otherFinancial, preciseLocation, coarseLocation, sensitiveInfo, contacts, emails, photos, audio, gameplay, support, otherContent, browsingHistory, searchHistory, userId, deviceId, purchaseHistory, productInteraction, advertisingData, otherUsage, crashData, performanceData, otherDiagnostic, environmentScanning, hands, head, otherData. google: { encryptedInTransit, deletionRequest, accountCreation: [usernamePassword|usernameOtherAuth|usernamePasswordOtherAuth|oauth|other] or ["none"], accountCreationOther, accountDeletionUrl (required with accounts) }. Kept in Ploa: Data safety goes to Google with ploa_play_data_safety_send (or the person's Send); App Privacy is entered by the person in App Store Connect.

dir.description: The app's folder (absolute path). Defaults to the folder the agent runs in.

tools.name: ploa_details_send
tools.description: Checks every answer against both stores' rules and, when nothing would be refused, sends every draft to App Store Connect and Google Play in one go, saying per part what each took. When something would be refused, nothing is sent and the problems come back with the step to fix each in. Apple keeps what's for a version with App Review (Ploa sends it once Apple decides); an agent's price change becomes an approval. Needs a token allowed to submit; otherwise tell the person to press Send on the Store details page.

dir.description: The app's folder (absolute path). Defaults to the folder the agent runs in.

tools.name: ploa_encryption_get
tools.description: Apple's export compliance for the app's iOS builds: the person's answers about the app's encryption (kept in Ploa), whether they need an encryption declaration at Apple and which document (a CCATS for proprietary algorithms; the French encryption declaration when it's sold in France), the declaration Ploa made and Apple's review state, the version's build's answer, what the Info.plist should say, and what's left with who does it. Includes each question in words to ask the person. Read-only.

fresh.description: Ask Apple again instead of the copy from the last two minutes.

dir.description: The app's folder (absolute path). Defaults to the folder the agent runs in.

tools.name: ploa_encryption_save
tools.description: Saves the person's answers about the app's encryption in Ploa (nothing reaches Apple until ploa_encryption_declare or the person's Send to Apple). These are the person's statements under US and French export rules: ask them, with what the code suggests (ploa_encryption_get has the questions), and save only what they said. kind: "none" (no encryption, or only Apple's: HTTPS through iOS, the Keychain) | "exempt" (only for what Category 5, Part 2 of the US rules exempts) | "standard" (standard algorithms the app implements itself, like a bundled OpenSSL or libsodium) | "proprietary" | "both". With standard, proprietary or both: france (true when it's on the App Store in France) and description (what the app is and what it uses encryption for). A change after a declaration was made means a new one is made when sent.

dir.description: The app's folder (absolute path). Defaults to the folder the agent runs in.

tools.name: ploa_encryption_document
tools.description: Uploads the document Apple asks for with an encryption declaration, from an absolute path on this machine (PDF, PNG or JPEG, up to 10 MB): the CCATS from the US Bureau of Industry and Security (proprietary algorithms) and/or the French encryption declaration (on the App Store in France). Only a document the person gave you: they come from those authorities, never write one. Apple takes one file per declaration, so two documents go in one PDF. Kept in Ploa and sent with the declaration.

dir.description: The app's folder (absolute path). Defaults to the folder the agent runs in.

tools.name: ploa_encryption_declare
tools.description: Sends the saved export compliance answers to Apple: when they need it, makes the encryption declaration in App Store Connect, uploads its document, and attaches it to the App Store version's build and the builds waiting for an answer (or the one buildId); otherwise answers "no non-exempt encryption" on those builds. Apple reviews a declaration (about two business days); Ploa attaches it to each new build it sees processed. It's the person's statement to Apple, so only a person sends it (on the Store details page) unless ploa_access says this agent is autonomous; otherwise this says where they press Send.

buildId.description: Only this build (its App Store Connect ID).

dir.description: The app's folder (absolute path). Defaults to the folder the agent runs in.

tools.name: ploa_screenshot_specs
tools.description: The stores' screenshot rules per device type, from Apple's and Google's own pages: the exact sizes (Apple) or the range (Google Play), how many a set holds, the format, the size to make, which sets each store asks for, and a simulator that captures each Apple size as is. Then, for the app in this folder, what its store page has per language and which screenshot sets it still needs. Also the videos the page has, which are optional (App Store app previews, Google Play's promo video): ask the person before making one. Start here before making screenshots; capture them with ploa_screenshot_capture, check them with ploa_screenshot_check, and upload with ploa_screenshot_upload.

store.description: One store; both when left out.

all.description: Apple's older devices, Mac, Apple TV, Vision Pro and Watch too.

dir.description: The app's folder (absolute path). Defaults to the folder the agent runs in.

tools.name: ploa_screenshot_check
tools.description: Checks image files on this machine (absolute paths) against a store's rules, from each file's own header: PNG or JPEG, no transparency, the size (Apple: exactly one of the device size's; Google Play: 320 to 3840 px a side, at most twice as long as wide; the feature graphic exactly 1024×500) and the file size. With type, against that device type, and says if there are more files than a set holds; without it, which of the store's types take each file as it is. Nothing is sent anywhere.

type.description: Apple's display type (APP_IPHONE_67, APP_IPAD_PRO_3GEN_129…) or Google Play's image type (phoneScreenshots, sevenInchScreenshots, tenInchScreenshots, featureGraphic; a Wear OS app's wearScreenshots, a TV app's tvScreenshots and tvBanner).

tools.name: ploa_screenshot_web
tools.description: Saves a screenshot of a page of the app's web build (a dev server like http://localhost:8081, or the web's testing address) at exactly a store's size, with Chrome or Edge in the background: an iPhone 6.9-inch (1320×2868) by default, an iPad, or a Google Play phone. It's the way to make iPhone screenshots on Windows or Linux, where there's no iOS Simulator, for an app whose web build is the same app (Expo, Flutter, React Native for web). Apple wants screenshots of the app itself in use: show the person the result and use it only when the web build looks like the iPhone app (no browser-only parts, the same screens). It doesn't navigate or tap: open each screen by its address (an Expo Router path). Then ploa_screenshot_check and ploa_screenshot_upload.

type.description: The store's display type: APP_IPHONE_67 (default), APP_IPHONE_65, APP_IPAD_PRO_3GEN_129, or Google Play's phoneScreenshots, sevenInchScreenshots, tenInchScreenshots.

folder.description: Where to save it (absolute path). Default: screenshots/ in the project.

waitMs.description: How long the page may load before the shot, in ms (default 4000, up to 20000).

dir.description: The app's folder (absolute path). Defaults to the folder the agent runs in.

tools.name: ploa_screenshot_capture
tools.description: Saves what a booted iOS Simulator (xcrun simctl) or Android emulator or device (adb screencap) shows now, as a PNG, and says which of the store's types take it as it is. It only captures: run the app and bring it to the screen first; nothing is installed, booted or launched. Saved under the app's store/screenshots/<platform>/ unless folder says otherwise; an alpha channel is removed, since the stores refuse transparency. Pick the device by name or ID when several are running; list: true only lists them. For Apple's sizes, capture on the simulator ploa_screenshot_specs names (an iPhone 17 Pro Max gives the 6.9-inch 1320×2868).

platform.description: Needed only when both an iOS Simulator and an Android device are running.

device.description: The simulator's name or UDID, or the Android device's serial or model.

list.description: Only list the running simulators and devices.

name.description: The file's name, like 01-home.png. Defaults to the device and the time.

dir.description: The app's folder (absolute path). Defaults to the folder the agent runs in.

tools.name: ploa_privacy_hints
tools.description: Reads this app's package.json, Expo config, Info.plist purpose strings, AndroidManifest permissions, the privacy manifests of the app and its SDKs, and its imports, and returns hints for Apple's App Privacy and Google Play's Data safety: each well-known SDK (analytics, crash reporting, ads, push, sign-in, payments…) and permission with the data types and purposes it usually involves, in the keys ploa_privacy_save takes. Each hint says where it was found, whether it collects by design or only depending on how the app uses it, and what to check in the code. Also flags tracking (ATT, the advertising ID), sharing with third parties, ads, account deletion when there is sign-in, and encryption in transit. Local and deterministic; it doesn't decide the answers.

dir.description: The app's folder (absolute path). Defaults to the folder the agent runs in.

tools.name: ploa_ask_person
tools.description: Puts a task in the person's approvals for something only a person can do, which you found is needed: a form or declaration in App Store Connect or Play Console that no store API takes (App Privacy, Play's App content forms, Apple's regulated medical device and EU trader declarations), an agreement only the Account Holder accepts, a click in a store's console. Ploa files these itself when a store stops a request (ploa_person_tasks lists them): ask for one only when it isn't there. Give it as numbered steps, each with the exact answer and, where it's done, its link and button words. The dashboard is in English or Hebrew and Ploa doesn't translate: steps and title in English, and he with the same in Hebrew. firstTimeOnly: true when only the first time is the person's and later times you or Ploa do it (a first release from a console). part: the store details part it is, when it's one of them (Did it then marks it done there too). Then walk the person through it in chat in their language, step by step with the links, and give them the task's address in Ploa that this returns. Never for something you can do yourself, and never to get around an approval.

title.description: A short title, in English (Declare the medical device status at Apple).

text.description: What to do in this step, with the exact answer to enter.

button.description: The button's words for the link (Open App Information).

text.description: What to do in this step, with the exact answer to enter.

button.description: The button's words for the link (Open App Information).

he.description: The same title and steps in Hebrew, for a dashboard in Hebrew.

link.description: The main page where it's done (https).

part.description: The store details part it is, when it's one of them.

firstTimeOnly.description: Only the first time is the person's; later times are done for them.

what.description: Instead of steps: the same as one text (older form).

dir.description: The app's folder (absolute path). Defaults to the folder the agent runs in.

tools.name: ploa_person_tasks
tools.description: The tasks waiting in the person's approvals for something only they can do (a store console's form, a declaration, Google's first production release in Play Console), the ones Ploa filed itself when a store stopped a request and the ones agents asked for: each with its numbered steps, their links, and its address in Ploa. Call it after a store refuses or holds something (a release left as a draft, App Review's refusal), and whenever the person asks what's left. Walk them through each in chat, step by step with the links, and give each task's address. Read-only.

dir.description: The app's folder (absolute path). Defaults to the folder the agent runs in.

tools.name: ploa_news
tools.description: What happened in the last week that you should know: a store's review answer (App Review, Google Play), a build that failed or reached testers, an approval the person decided, a person's task done, something a store turned down, a low review, a TestFlight build about to expire, a store connection that stopped working. Each with what to do next. New ones also come at the end of any Ploa tool's answer, once; call this at the start of the work, and when the person asks what's new.

tools.name: ploa_what_now
tools.description: The home page's What now for every app of the workspace in one call: the requests waiting for a person's approval (App Review, production, prices, testers, files), the builds and steps that failed or stopped, and what's on its way. Use it at the start of the work and when the person asks what's going on; for one app's stores in detail, ploa_shipping_report.

tools.name: ploa_activity
tools.description: What was done in this app, newest first, from Ploa's audit log: store details sent, builds and releases, approvals asked and decided, keys and settings changed, each with who did it (a person, an agent by name, a token, or Ploa itself) and when. Use it when picking up work another session or person started, or when the person asks who changed something.

dir.description: The app's folder (absolute path). Defaults to the folder the agent runs in.

tools.name: ploa_gap_report
tools.description: Writes down for Ploa's own team something Ploa doesn't do or got wrong, that this work ran into: a store form it doesn't fill, a check that fired for nothing, a step that had to be done by hand. Say what happened, what was done instead, and what would fix it. It goes to Ploa's operators, not to the person, and doesn't ask anyone; use it instead of quietly working around a gap. Nothing secret: no keys, passwords or customers' data. A few a day per workspace.

title.description: One line: what Ploa doesn't do (up to 200 characters).

details.description: What happened, what was done instead, and what would fix it (up to 8000 characters).

dir.description: The app's folder (absolute path). Defaults to the folder the agent runs in.

tools.name: ploa_support_request
tools.description: Drafts a message to Ploa's support for the person to approve: a problem with Ploa itself, billing, a refund, privacy. Agents never write to support themselves, so it waits for the person, and goes out under their name and email once they approve it on ploa.dev (never in advance, not even for an autonomous agent). Put in what support needs: what was tried, the app, the release or run ID, and the error word for word. For something Ploa doesn't cover that needs no answer, ploa_gap_report.

message.description: The message, as the person would send it.

dir.description: The app's folder (absolute path). Defaults to the folder the agent runs in.

tools.name: ploa_store_deadlines
tools.description: The App Store's and Google Play's rules with a date that Ploa knows (the Xcode a build must come from, Google Play's target SDK, Play's trader status), and each app of the workspace against them: its newest Android build's target SDK next to the one Google asks for now. Use it before planning a release, and when the person asks what's coming.

tools.name: ploa_min_version
tools.description: Sets the lowest version of this app people may keep using, per platform, without an SDK: the app asks Ploa at start (GET https://ploa.dev/api/v1/min-version/<app ID>?platform=ios&version=<its version>, no sign-in) and gets update: true below it, with the message and the store's link to show. Without minVersion it only reads what's set; minVersion null stops asking. The answer gives the address and a few lines of code for the app to call it. Use it when a version has a bug people must leave, or an old API is going away.

message.description: What the app shows, in the app's main language (up to 300 characters).

dir.description: The app's folder (absolute path). Defaults to the folder the agent runs in.

tools.name: ploa_schedule_release
tools.description: Asks a person to approve releasing at a set time, on one store or both together: iosReleaseId puts the version App Review approved onto the App Store (its release option must be manual: ploa_appstore_release_type), androidReleaseId sends the build to production on Google Play (rolloutPercent for a staged rollout). Once approved, each waits and goes out at its time (up to 30 days ahead); Google still reviews an Android release first, so send Android a day or two early or schedule it after Google approved. at is a time with its zone, like 2026-11-10T10:00:00+02:00. Follow each request with ploa_approval_status.

at.description: When, as an ISO time with its zone (2026-11-10T10:00:00+02:00).

iosReleaseId.description: The iOS release whose approved version goes onto the App Store.

androidReleaseId.description: The Android release that goes to production.

rolloutPercent.description: Android only: the share of users, 1 to 100. Default 100.

tools.name: ploa_size_report
tools.description: Each recent build's size per platform (the .ipa and .aab the build machine sent), with the change from the build before it, and a warning when an iPhone build passes 200 MB, past which iPhones ask before downloading it over cellular data. Use it after a build that grew, or before adding a big dependency or asset.

dir.description: The app's folder (absolute path). Defaults to the folder the agent runs in.

tools.name: ploa_review_rejection
tools.description: Everything the App Store and Google Play said when they turned something down, in one place: the App Store version (REJECTED, METADATA_REJECTED, INVALID_BINARY), builds Apple's processing refused, TestFlight beta review, in-app purchases and subscriptions, in-app events, custom product pages and tests, Google Play releases its review didn't approve, and releases or approved requests the store refused on the way. Each with its state, when, every reason the stores' APIs give, the message the person pasted from App Store Connect or Play Console with its guideline numbers and ITMS codes, the link where the full text is, and what to do next. Apple's API has no App Review message or guideline numbers, and Google's none for policy rejections: when the person gives you that text, pass it as text (with item, the rejection's key from this tool, or store) and Ploa keeps it with the rejection, in the audit log. Start here when an app was rejected.

text.description: The store's message as the person copied it (App Store Connect › App Review, or Play Console's Inbox), to keep in Ploa. Up to 20000 characters.

item.description: Which rejection the text belongs to: its key from this tool (like apple:version:…). Leave out for the store's newest.

store.description: With text and no item: whose message it is.

he.description: The message in Hebrew, faithful and complete, guideline numbers and names of things left as they are.

translations.description: The message translated, for people who read Ploa in that language; the store's own text is kept as it is. With text, or with note for a message already kept.

note.description: With translations: the id of a message already kept (shown as note … in this tool's answer).

fresh.description: Ask the stores again instead of the answer from the last ten minutes.

dir.description: The app's folder (absolute path). Defaults to the folder the agent runs in.

tools.name: ploa_app_review_reply
tools.description: Keeps the developer's reply to App Review's message after an App Store rejection, for when the message waits for an answer (it asks for information or a question, like Guideline 2.1 Information Needed; ploa_app_review_status and ploa_review_rejection say so) or the person disagrees with it. A rejection that asks for a fix needs no reply: the fixed build or store page is the answer, and ploa_release_submit_review sends it back without any text. The reply is sent before the version goes back to App Review: once it does, App Store Connect closes the thread (no reply box), and Ploa then refuses a new draft and closes one not sent. The person sends it in one step: it shows on the app's Release page under the version, with Copy reply, a link to that submission's thread in App Store Connect › App Review, and I sent it. Apple's API has no way to send a message in App Review's thread, so Ploa never sends it there and nothing reaches Apple from this tool: the person pastes it and presses Send in App Store Connect. To have App Review read it with a resubmission too, pass the reply's id as replyId to ploa_release_submit_review: under that approval Ploa puts it in the version's App Review Information › Notes. Write the reply in English, short and factual, answering what App Review asked (what changed in the build, where the reviewer finds it), from ploa_review_rejection's message and the app's code; show it to the person before you keep it. A newer draft for the same version replaces the one not sent yet. With sent and the reply's id, keeps it as sent once the person says they sent it.

text.description: The reply, in English, as it goes to App Review. Up to 4000 characters (what App Review Information › Notes takes).

he.description: The reply in Hebrew, for a person who reads Ploa in Hebrew; the English one is what goes to Apple.

translations.description: The reply translated, shown beside it to people who read Ploa in that language.

version.description: The App Store version it's about, like 1.0.0. Leave out for the newest rejected one.

item.description: Or the rejection's key from ploa_review_rejection (apple:version:…).

submission.description: The review submission's ID at App Store Connect, when the rejection is no longer in ploa_review_rejection (the version was resubmitted): the link then opens its thread.

sent.description: Instead of text: the id of a reply the person sent in App Store Connect, to keep it as sent.

dir.description: The app's folder (absolute path). Defaults to the folder the agent runs in.

tools.name: ploa_app_review_status
tools.description: Where the app's App Store version stands with App Review now, from App Store Connect: its state (waiting, in review, approved and waiting for release, released in phases, rejected), its build, its release option and phased release (day of 7, paused), the newest build on TestFlight that can go to App Review, what App Review decided before (approved or rejected, and when), the requests waiting for a person, and the next steps with the tool and release ID for each. Ploa hears App Review's answer within minutes and tells the person on their devices. For what App Review said in a rejection, use ploa_review_rejection.

fresh.description: Ask App Store Connect now instead of what Ploa read in the last minute.

dir.description: The app's folder (absolute path). Defaults to the folder the agent runs in.

tools.name: ploa_appstore_release_type
tools.description: Asks a person to approve changing the newest App Store version's release option: AFTER_APPROVAL (Apple releases it as soon as App Review approves it) or MANUAL (it waits, Pending Developer Release, until a person releases it with ploa_appstore_release). Apple takes a change until it approves the version; after that it's refused with why. A scheduled date is set with ploa_details_save (review.releaseType SCHEDULED). Nothing changes at Apple until a person approves on the Ploa dashboard (unless ploa_access says this agent is autonomous); check it with ploa_approval_status. ploa_app_review_status says the option now.

dir.description: The app's folder (absolute path). Defaults to the folder the agent runs in.

tools.name: ploa_play_review_status
tools.description: Where the app's newest production release stands with Google Play's review now (in review, approved and held by managed publishing, not approved, published, a staged rollout's share), the newer build that can go in its place, Google's decisions before, the requests waiting for a person, the next steps with the tool for each, and managed publishing as far as Ploa can tell. Google's API can't read or change managed publishing, or publish a release it holds: Ploa knows it's on once Google has held an approved release, and turning it on or off and publishing are the person's step in Play Console › Publishing overview (the link is in the answer; say plainly that Ploa can't do it). Read-only.

fresh.description: Ask Google Play now (it has a daily limit per app; Ploa reads a few times a day by itself).

dir.description: The app's folder (absolute path). Defaults to the folder the agent runs in.

tools.name: ploa_appstore_release
tools.description: Asks a person to approve releasing an iOS version App Review approved and that waits for the developer (Pending Developer Release, the release option "manually release"): Apple then puts it on the App Store, for everyone or, with a phased release, to a growing share of people with automatic updates over 7 days. Pass the release of its build (ploa_app_review_status gives it). A version that isn't approved yet, or that Apple releases by itself, is refused with why. Nothing reaches Apple until a person approves on the Ploa dashboard; check it with ploa_approval_status. Needs a token allowed to touch production. Google Play uses ploa_release_promote.

releaseId.description: The release ID that ploa_release_start returned.

tools.name: ploa_appstore_phased_release
tools.description: Asks a person to approve a change to an App Store version's phased release (7 days, to a growing share of people with automatic updates): pause (they stop getting it; anyone can still download it from the App Store; Apple allows 30 days of pauses in all), resume (a paused one goes on from its day), or complete (everyone gets it now). Pass the release of the version's build (ploa_app_review_status gives it and says which of these apply). Nothing changes at Apple until a person approves on the Ploa dashboard; check it with ploa_approval_status. Needs a token allowed to touch production.

releaseId.description: The release ID that ploa_release_start returned.

instructions:
Ploa takes this app to the App Store and Google Play.
A new app, or a store or Ploa not set up yet: start with ploa_setup_guide. It says what's left, in order, who does each step (the person or you) and the links, and suggests the app's ID (bundle ID and package name) when there's none. Ask the person as few times as you can: their questions and their steps for both stores (and GitHub, if builds run there) go together in one numbered message, in their language and with the links, since none waits on another. Do yours meanwhile (ploa_link, ploa_appstore_register_bundle_id) and run the guide again after each.
How you work is the person's choice, asked once at the start: until they've chosen, ploa_setup_guide opens with the question (an autonomous agent, or approvals, with what each means). Ask it before anything else and record their answer with ploa_access (choose). You can never make yourself autonomous: for that, pass on the link ploa_access gives, where they confirm it in Ploa.
Ask, don't assume: the store page's languages, the countries the app is in, its price, who it's for, App Review's contact (private) and the store page's contact (public) are the person's decisions; one given for the first is never used for the second. Ask them (ploa_setup_guide lists the questions with what the code suggests) and wait for the answers before saving any of it.
Don't wait while the person works in the consoles: write the store details and privacy answers (they're saved as drafts before the store has the app), make the screenshots, and check the iOS build on this Mac with ploa release ios --no-upload (built and signed by Ploa, not sent) and the Android build with ploa release android --no-upload (built and checked, not sent). Both stores need a privacy policy and a support page at https addresses: an app without a site of its own can have them on its web on Ploa (privacy.html and support.html in the web project's public folder, Flutter's web/; ploa_web_setup with the address the person picks, then ploa_web_build, gives https://<address>.ploa.app/privacy.html).
After ploa update, the Ploa tools an agent already started still run the old version until the agent restarts or reloads its MCP servers; their answers say so when it happens.
Keep the person oriented: at the start of the work show them the stages board from ploa_setup_guide, and after every step show it again with what was just done (and by whom: you, them or Ploa), what's left, what's needed from them, and what Ploa updates in the stores by itself.
Whatever only the person can do (a console form, a declaration, an agreement, Google's first production release in Play Console) is a task in their approvals: Ploa files one itself when a store stops a request, and you ask for one with ploa_ask_person when it isn't there; ploa_person_tasks lists them. Whenever there's one, on either store, walk the person through it in chat in their language, step by step with each step's link, and give its address in Ploa (/app/approvals?task=<id>), where the same steps have buttons and Did it marks it done. After a store refuses or holds something, call ploa_person_tasks before anything else.
Say plainly what Ploa can't update: Apple's App Privacy and Play Console's App content forms other than Data safety are entered by the person in the store's console (Apple has no API for keys or for creating the app either; the guide says what to do). For each, tell them what to enter and where (ploa_details_get lists each with its answers and link; the Store details page's Privacy step has them too), and that they tick it there once done. An app that sells anything needs Apple's Paid Applications Agreement, with tax and banking, which only the Account Holder accepts (no API either). Export compliance (the app's encryption, for every iOS build) is the person's statement: read the code and suggest, ask them (ploa_encryption_get has the questions), save their answers, and Ploa makes Apple's encryption declaration when they send it.
Every instruction for the person comes from ploa_setup_guide: a certificate, a capability to turn on at Apple, a console form, a key. When a tool's error asks something of the person, run the guide and pass on its step rather than your own wording. Give every link as a clickable markdown link, [name](https://…), as the guide writes them; never an address or a path to type.
Usual order once set up: ploa_preflight (fix what it finds), then ploa_release_start, then ploa_release_status until the build is on TestFlight or internal testing. Ploa builds Expo, Flutter, React Native (with or without Expo), Capacitor, Android (Gradle) and Xcode apps itself, each with its own tools; another kind (Unity, .NET MAUI...) ships as it's built, with ploa release android --aab <file> or ploa release ios --ipa <file>.
To stop a build that's still building: ploa_release_stop says what stopping does where it runs; show the person, and call it again with confirm: true only once they say yes.
To build without this machine (no Mac needed for Android), run ploa_github_status; ploa_github_setup does your part and asks the person for theirs (linking the repository is their approval); ploa_github_settings asks them to approve a change to the app's GitHub settings (PR labels, iOS on GitHub's Macs, Releases on GitHub, the store page from the repo, issues from the stores). ploa_release_start with where: "auto" builds on GitHub once it's ready there. Before an iOS build on GitHub's Macs, say it uses the person's GitHub minutes.
App Review and production need a person: ploa_release_submit_review (replace: true sends a newer build in place of the one with App Review; a version App Review rejected goes back with it too, with a new build or the same, never by hand in App Store Connect), ploa_release_withdraw_review, ploa_release_promote (Google Play), ploa_appstore_release (the version App Review approved, onto the App Store) and ploa_appstore_phased_release (pause, resume or finish its phased release) only ask, and ploa_approval_status tells you the answer. ploa_app_review_status says where the version stands with App Review and what's next; Ploa hears App Review's answer within minutes and tells the person. ploa_play_review_status says the same for Google Play's review, with managed publishing: Google has no API for it, so turning it on or off and publishing a release it holds are the person's, in Play Console (say so plainly, with the link). ploa_appstore_release_type asks to change whether Apple releases the version when it approves it or a person does. Wait for it; never try another way around an approval. If the person made this agent autonomous (ploa_access says so), the same tools carry it out at once instead, approved in advance, and everything is still recorded under the agent's name.
To see where everything stands (builds, submissions, the last run): ploa_shipping_report. ploa_runs shows each release step by step.
The web is a platform of the app too, with Ploa as its store (Ploa Aio): ploa_web_status shows each app's web (a web app, pages about the app, or both; a PWA or not) and its versions; ploa_web_setup adds the web to an app (ask the person for its address and what it is first). ploa_web_build builds it in the project with its own framework (Expo, Next static export, Vite, Astro, SvelteKit, Nuxt, Angular, Flutter and more; a site with a server side is refused, as hosting is static for now) and sends the built folder as a new version: Ploa numbers it, checks it and puts it at its own testing address for the site's testers (ploa_web_testers). When the person says it's good, ploa_web_release puts it live, which a person approves unless you're autonomous; ploa_web_rollback goes back at once. Every site has a free <address>.ploa.app; Ploa sells no domains, and ploa_web_domain_add connects one the person already owns (it returns the DNS records they add), ploa_web_domain_check says whether it's connected.
The store details (text, screenshots, category, age rating, price, App Review's contact, privacy) are yours to write: Ploa has no AI of its own. They're one set of answers for both stores: start from ploa_details_get, read the app's code to know what it does, save with ploa_details_save (many languages at once) and ploa_privacy_save, and fix what each store would refuse. A person checks and sends it all with one click on ploa.dev; send yourself (ploa_details_send) only if ploa_access says you're autonomous. Videos (App Store app previews, Google Play's promo video) are optional, never required: ask the person whether they want one before making it.
While Apple has something with App Review (the app's version, a product, an event), a change to it (an image, screenshots, text) is kept in Ploa and sent by Ploa once Apple has decided: the tool says "Kept in Ploa". That's done as far as you're concerned; don't retry it or look for another way. ploa_held_changes lists what's kept and, with send: true, sends it now (after App Review has decided, or when the person asks), which waits for a person's approval unless ploa_access says you're autonomous.
What happened while you weren't asking (a store's review answer, a build that failed or reached testers, an approval the person decided, a person's task done, something a store turned down, a low review, a TestFlight build about to expire, a broken store connection) comes at the end of your next Ploa tool's answer under "News from Ploa", once each: tell the person what matters to them and do what each line says. ploa_news lists the last week's; call it at the start of the work.
Step-by-step briefs are this server's prompts: set_up_app, fill_store_page, translate_store_page, make_screenshots, answer_privacy, handle_rejection, write_release_notes.
